intro: RRSP, TFSA, FHSA, and other registered plans affect nearly every Canadian's T1 return. Let's make sure your contributions, deductions, and repayment obligations are all captured.

screens.title: Did you contribute to an RRSP in 2025 or within 60 days of January 1, 2026?
screens.instruction: RRSP contributions are deductible under ITA s.146(1) up to your deduction limit shown on your Notice of Assessment. Contributions made from January 1, 2025 to March 1, 2026 can be claimed on your 2025 return.

true.message: RRSP contributions reduce your taxable income dollar for dollar up to your deduction limit. Your limit is shown on your most recent Notice of Assessment. Contribution receipts are mailed by your financial institution — also available through CRA My Account. Note: you do not have to deduct the full contribution in 2025 — unused contributions can be carried forward to future years when your marginal rate may be higher.

document_checklist_add.document: RRSP contribution receipts for all contributions from March 2, 2025 to March 1, 2026

false.message: No RRSP contributions in 2025. Unused RRSP room accumulates indefinitely — check your most recent Notice of Assessment for your available room.

screens.title: Do you want to deduct the full RRSP contribution on your 2025 return?
screens.instruction: You can contribute to an RRSP now but carry the deduction forward to a future year when your income — and marginal tax rate — may be higher. This is a legitimate and often beneficial planning strategy.

options.label: Yes — deduct the full contribution on my 2025 return
No — I want to carry forward some or all of the deduction
I want my preparer to advise on the optimal timing

false.message: Carrying forward the RRSP deduction is noted. This is beneficial if your income is expected to be higher in a future year — the deduction saves more tax at a higher marginal rate. Your preparer will note the carry-forward amount.

preparer_flag.flag: Client prefers to carry forward some or all RRSP deduction — model optimal deduction year based on income projections

discuss.message: Your preparer will model the deduction timing based on your current and projected future income to maximise tax savings.

preparer_flag.flag: Model RRSP deduction timing — compare current year vs future year tax saving based on marginal rates

screens.title: Did you contribute to a spousal RRSP in 2025?
screens.instruction: A spousal RRSP contribution uses your own deduction room but builds retirement savings in your spouse's name — useful for equalising retirement income and reducing total tax through pension splitting.

true.message: Spousal RRSP contributions are deductible on your return using your own RRSP room. However, if your spouse withdraws from the spousal RRSP within 3 calendar years of any spousal contribution, the withdrawal is attributed back to you as income under ITA s.146(8.3) — the attribution rule. Your preparer must track the last spousal contribution date.

document_checklist_add.document: Spousal RRSP contribution receipt and record of last spousal contribution date — required to assess 3-year attribution rule under ITA s.146(8.3)

preparer_flag.flag: Spousal RRSP contribution — record date of last contribution for 3-year attribution rule under ITA s.146(8.3)

screens.title: Do you have a First Home Savings Account (FHSA)?
screens.instruction: FHSA contributions under ITA s.146.6 are tax-deductible regardless of whether you purchased a home in 2025. The annual limit is $8,000 with a lifetime maximum of $40,000. Unused room carries forward by $8,000 per year.

options.label: Yes — I contributed to an FHSA in 2025
Yes — I made a qualifying withdrawal to purchase my first home
I opened an FHSA in 2025 but did not contribute yet

contributed.message: FHSA contributions are deductible on your 2025 T1 under ITA s.146.6. The annual limit is $8,000 — if you opened your FHSA in 2023 or earlier and did not use your full room, you may have up to $16,000 available in 2025. Your financial institution will issue an FHSA contribution receipt.

document_checklist_add.document: FHSA contribution receipt from financial institution — shows 2025 contributions deductible on T1

withdrew.message: A qualifying FHSA withdrawal to purchase a first home is completely tax-free under ITA s.146.6 — no income inclusion and no repayment required. You must have been a first-time buyer and the home must close by October 1 of the year following the withdrawal. A T4FHSA slip will be issued. We will cover the full purchase detail in the First Home section.

document_checklist_add.document: T4FHSA — Statement of First Home Savings Account showing contributions and qualifying withdrawal amount

opened_only.message: Opening an FHSA without contributing preserves future room. No deduction is available for 2025, but you can contribute up to $8,000 in 2026 plus any carry-forward room accumulated since opening.

false.message: No FHSA noted. If you are a first-time buyer under 71, you may still be eligible to open one — contributions are deductible and qualifying withdrawals are tax-free. Your preparer can advise on eligibility.

preparer_flag.flag: Assess FHSA eligibility — client may qualify to open and deduct contributions if a first-time buyer under 71

screens.title: Did you have any involvement with an RESP withdrawal in 2025?
screens.instruction: RESP Educational Assistance Payments (EAPs) — which include accumulated income and government grants — are taxable in the student's hands under ITA s.146.1(7). The tax treatment depends on whether you are the student beneficiary or the subscriber who opened the plan.

options.label: I am the student — I received Educational Assistance Payments from an RESP
I am the subscriber — my child or grandchild received EAP payments

student.message: EAPs are taxable in your hands as the student beneficiary under ITA s.146.1(7). You will receive a T4A slip showing the EAP amount — this must be reported on your T1. Since most students have low income, tax on EAPs is often nil or minimal. The return of original RESP contributions to the subscriber is always tax-free and does not affect your return.

document_checklist_add.document: T4A slip — Statement of RESP Educational Assistance Payment issued to you as the student beneficiary

subscriber.message: As the subscriber, the EAP income belongs to the student — there is nothing to report on your T1 from the withdrawal itself. Confirm that the student beneficiary has received their T4A and will report the EAP on their own return.

preparer_flag.flag: RESP EAP withdrawal made by subscriber — confirm student beneficiary has T4A and will report EAP income on their own T1 under ITA s.146.1(7)

screens.title: Do any of the following registered plan repayment obligations apply to you?
screens.instruction: These obligations arise from RRSP withdrawals made in prior years. Missed annual repayments are added to your income for that year — they are not optional.

options.label: I am repaying a Home Buyers' Plan (HBP) withdrawal from a prior year
I am repaying a Lifelong Learning Plan (LLP) withdrawal from a prior year

hbp_repayment.message: HBP repayments are made by contributing to your own RRSP and designating the amount on Schedule 7 — they are not separate payments to CRA. Your annual required repayment amount is shown on your Notice of Assessment. If you do not make the required repayment, that year's shortfall is added to your income under ITA s.146.01. Bring your NOA and confirm your repayment amount with your preparer.

document_checklist_add.document: Notice of Assessment — confirms annual HBP repayment amount required for 2025. Schedule 7 must be filed to designate RRSP contributions as HBP repayments.

preparer_flag.flag: HBP repayment obligation — confirm annual required amount from NOA and whether repayment was made via RRSP contribution designated on Schedule 7

llp_repayment.message: LLP repayments work the same way as HBP — contribute to your RRSP and designate the amount on Schedule 7. Your annual required repayment is shown on your Notice of Assessment. Missed repayments are added to your income under ITA s.146.02. Repayments must begin no later than 10 years after the first LLP withdrawal, or the year after you cease to be a full-time student — whichever is earlier.

document_checklist_add.document: Notice of Assessment — confirms annual LLP repayment amount required for 2025. Schedule 7 must be filed to designate RRSP contributions as LLP repayments.

preparer_flag.flag: LLP repayment obligation — confirm annual required amount from NOA and whether repayment was made via RRSP contribution designated on Schedule 7

none.message: No prior registered plan repayment obligations noted.

branch_completion_summary.message:
Savings and registered plans section complete.

Reminder: Over-contributions to registered accounts are not resolved through your T1 — they require separate CRA filings. Raise any concerns with your preparer: RRSP excess above $2,000 buffer → Form T1-OVP by March 31, 2026 (ITA s.204.1); TFSA excess → Form RC243 by June 30, 2026 (ITA s.207.02); FHSA excess → Form RC243-SCH-A by June 30, 2026 (ITA s.207.021); RESP excess above $50,000 per beneficiary → Form T1E-OVP by June 30, 2026 (ITA s.204.9). Verify all contribution room via CRA My Account.
highlighted_documents: RRSP contribution receipts for March 2025 to March 2026 period
Notice of Assessment — confirms RRSP deduction limit, HBP/LLP repayment amounts, and TFSA room
Spousal RRSP receipt and last contribution date record
FHSA contribution receipt or T4FHSA slip
T4A slip — RESP Educational Assistance Payment (issued to student beneficiary)
